resources.string: Restart the router
It turns off and back on, keeping everything
Factory reset
Erases everything and leaves it as it came out of the box
This router doesn\'t allow it from the app
While it starts up, there\'s no internet or Wi-Fi at home.
Cancel
Restart the router?
It turns off and back on, without losing any settings. For a minute or two there will be no internet or Wi-Fi at home.
You\'re away from home: the app signs back in by itself once it starts, but if it didn\'t come back, nothing could be done from here.
Restart
Restarting the router…
It takes a minute or two. The app signs back in by itself once it starts.
The router is back
The router isn\'t answering yet
Several minutes have passed. Check that its lights are on; if it doesn\'t come back, unplug it for a few seconds and plug it back in.
Factory reset?

Everything you set up is erased: the password, the Wi-Fi, the internet connection, the profiles, remote access and anything installed. For a few minutes there will be no internet, and then it has to be set up again (if your internet provider gave you a username and password, keep them at hand).
It goes back to its factory address (on OpenWrt, 192.168.1.1) with no password. If it comes with Wi-Fi off from the factory, like OpenWrt, you\'ll need a cable.
You\'re away from home: afterwards you can only get in from home.
I understand everything is erased
Erase everything
Resetting the router…
The router couldn\'t erase its settings: nothing has changed.

The router is going back to factory settings: it takes a few minutes. Then connect the phone to it (through its factory Wi-Fi or a cable) and sign in at its factory address (on OpenWrt, 192.168.1.1) with no password: the app helps you set it up.
